correctness.rationale: Exact three-state substochastic chain and strictly positive finite-step meeting probability justify unique first-step equations. Algebra gives the three rational means, common positive comparison denominator, strict root monotonicity, endpoint signs, sharp lower bound and degenerate cases for every m>=s>=1 with m>=2 and p in (0,1). The separately constructed full-pair exact rational solver passed 31129 assertions, including graph instances with singleton parts; finite verification is corroborative, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed novelty is the all-size complete classification of which initial pair class meets first or last in mean as the holding probability varies, including two sharp roots and the universal p=1/3 balanced equality. Closest same-model paper (Alpern–Zeng 2021) treats other graph families, and general bounds/spectral expressions neither state nor directly cover these exact threshold signs. Published-result semantic searches and accessible own prior claims showed no implying statement. value.rationale: A motivated rendezvous-comparison problem is completely classified across all graph sizes and all admissible holding probabilities: every initial pair in complete bipartite graphs falls into a provably ordered type. Two separated sharp phase boundaries govern minimum/maximum mean meeting delay in unbalanced bicliques; at p=1/3 every distinct start has equal mean 9m/4 in balanced bicliques; universal threshold bounds and extremal asymptotics quantify the structural effect. This is a natural complete infinite-family classification, not an arbitrary single numerical instance or a restatement of the absorbing-chain formula.
